Lisa — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short proposal (Acme_Proposal_v3.pdf) and a reconciliation workbook (AM_reconciliation_template.xlsx) that maps a frontloaded wallet vs a stepped ramp. High level options:

Option A — Frontloaded prepay (preferred by Acme):
- Year 1: 60% of total committed $ wired up front (frontloaded credit \"shelf\")
- Years 2–3: 20% prepay each year up front
- Term discount: 15% off list for 3-year committed spend (tiered to 18% if ARR > $5M)
- Monthly reconciliation: auto-apply usage against wallet; finance gets a monthly statement and variance report
- Unused credit policy: credits roll forward for up to 12 months after each anniversary; any remaining balance beyond 12 months is eligible for a 50% refundable credit (subject to audit)

Option B — Stepped ramp drawdown:
- Year 1: 30% prepay; Year 2: 35%; Year 3: 35%
- Term discount: 12% (3-year); unspent credits roll forward for 6 months only
- Lower up-front cash but higher monthly exposure (we can still set monthly floors)

Operational notes:
- We support monthly reconciliation exports / GL-friendly CSVs and a one-line invoice for month-end true-ups
- For underuse protection, Redwood offers a partial buyback for unused credits at 50% of unused value if usage is < 70% of committed across a rolling 12 months
- If Acme needs to accelerate drawdown, we can front-apply credits to spikes but that reduces monthly committed floor calculations (we will document exceptions)

Attachments: Acme_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal, 8 pages); AM_reconciliation_template.xlsx (reconciliation workbook)
